request.description: Train a fresh baseline policy under the current training distribution to obtain the first frozen candidate for reach-to-hold diagnosis.
request.rationale: There is no candidate or campaign evidence yet. This run establishes a reproducible behavioral baseline that can be evaluated by target radius and angle using first reach, longest hold, interruptions, and binary success. Those measurements discriminate failure to reach or transfer from stabilization failure; training return alone cannot establish the human goal.

request.description: Evaluate the two strongest late baseline checkpoints on the same 160-episode official-distribution development panel, retaining per-episode reach and hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: Training success was measured on the outer-radius training distribution and cannot distinguish transfer failure from stabilization failure. A paired official-distribution panel for the 0.97 and 0.95 late checkpoints will compare target-radius and angle effects, first reach, longest hold, interruptions, and binary success under identical episode seeds. This directly tests whether later training improved the relevant objective and identifies whether the next intervention should target coverage, control/stabilization, or neither yet.

scientific_session.objective: Establish the most credible initial scientific direction toward the human goal from the scientific model and available evidence. Use scientific work in this session to establish or refine that direction, including building or adapting reusable scientific tools and PI-owned methods where needed. These capabilities can support subsequent inquiries. Choose the first useful scientific action and explain why it advances the direction. Preserve the work actually performed, resulting understanding, remaining uncertainties and chosen next action in the scientific session record.
